en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 20.8.
Piṭṭhiduka (The Supplementary Couplets)
Dependent on a state not to be abandoned by vision, a state not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root condition … one.
Dependent on a state not to be abandoned by vision, a state to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state not to be abandoned by vision, a state not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state to be abandoned by vision (*dassanena pahātabba*), states both to be abandoned by vision and not to be abandoned by vision arise by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*) … three.
Dependent on a state both not to be abandoned by vision and not to be abandoned by vision, a state not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root condition … one. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, five; in the object condition, two ... pe ... in the result condition, one ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, five.
Dependent on a state not to be abandoned by cultivation, there arises a state not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. In the case of the root condition, five;
in the object condition, two ... pe ... in the result condition, one ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, five.

Dependent on a state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing (*dassanena pahātabba-hetuka*), a state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are nine;
under object [condition], six; under predominance [condition], five ... pe ... under result [condition], one ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition], nine.

Dependent on a state rooted in what is not to be abandoned by cultivation (*na-bhāvanāya pahātabba-hetuka*), a state rooted in what is to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause condition (hetu-paccaya), there are nine; in the object condition (ārammaṇa), six; in the predominance condition (adhipati), five …pe… in the result condition (vipāka), one …pe… in the non-disappearance condition (avigata), nine.
Dependent on a state without applied thought (na-savitakka), a state with applied thought (savitakka) arises by way of the root-cause condition.
Dependent on a state without applied thought, a state without applied thought arises by way of the root-cause condition. Dependent on a state without applied thought …pe… [and so forth].
States with applied thought and without applied thought arise by way of root condition... three.
Dependent on a state without applied thought, a state without applied thought arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state without applied thought, a state with applied thought arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state without applied thought, a state with applied thought...
And with neither initial application nor sustained application, states arise by way of root condition... three.
Dependent on a state that has neither initial application nor sustained application, a state with initial application arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that has neither initial application nor sustained application, a state without initial application arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on states with applied thought and without applied thought, there arise states both with applied thought and without applied thought by way of root condition ...
three. (Abbreviated. Nine for root;
nine for object ... pe ... six for prenascence and repetition ... pe ... nine for non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state with sustained application (*savicāra*), a state with sustained application arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
(Abbreviated. Nine [ways] under root; nine under object (*ārammaṇa*) ... pe ... six under prenascence (*purejāta*) and repetition (*āsevana*) ... pe ... nine under non-disappearance (*avigata*).
Dependent on a state without rapture (*nappītika*), a state with rapture (*sappītiko*) arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to the root condition, there are nine; with respect to the object condition, nine ... pe ... with respect to the prenascence and repetition conditions, six ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, nine.
Dependent on a state accompanied by rapture (*pītisahagata*), a state accompanied by rapture arises by way of the root condition.

(Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, there are nine; with respect to the object condition, nine ... pe ... with respect to the prenascence and repetition conditions, six ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, nine.
Dependent on a state accompanied by pleasure, a state accompanied by pleasure arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine under root; nine under object … pe … six under prenascence and repetition … pe … nine under non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state accompanied by equanimity, a state accompanied by equanimity arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state not accompanied by equanimity, a state not accompanied by equanimity arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state not accompanied by equanimity, states both accompanied by equanimity and not accompanied by equanimity arise by way of root condition… three.
Dependent on a state accompanied by equanimity, a state not accompanied by equanimity arises by way of root condition … three [cases].

Dependent on a state both not accompanied by equanimity and not accompanied by equanimity, a state accompanied by equanimity arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state both not accompanied by equanimity and not accompanied by equanimity … [and so forth].
A state accompanied by equanimity arises conditioned by a root cause.

Dependent on states both not accompanied by equanimity and not unaccompanied by equanimity, states both accompanied by equanimity and not unaccompanied by equanimity arise conditioned by a root cause… three. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause condition (hetu-paccaya), there are nine; in the case of object condition (ārammaṇa), nine … pe … in the case of prenascence and repetition conditions (purejāta-āsevana), six … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition (avigata), nine.

Dependent on a state not belonging to the sense-sphere (nakāmāvacara), a state belonging to the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara) arises by way of root-cause condition. Dependent on a state not belonging to the sense-sphere, a state not belonging to the sense-sphere arises by way of root-cause condition. Dependent on a state not belonging to the sense-sphere … [and so forth].
Dependent on [states] that are both sense-sphere and not sense-sphere, states that are both sense-sphere and not sense-sphere arise by way of root condition... three.
Dependent on a state that is not sense-sphere, a state that is not sense-sphere arises by way of root condition... three.
Dependent on a state that is both not sense-sphere and not not sense-sphere, a state that is sense-sphere arises by way of root condition... three. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root condition, nine; with respect to object condition, four; with respect to predominance condition, five …pe… with respect to mutuality condition, six …pe… with respect to prenascence and repetition conditions, two …pe… with respect to non-disappearance condition, nine.
Dependent on a state not belonging to the fine-material sphere, a state belonging to the fine-material sphere arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to root condition, nine;

with respect to object condition, four; with respect to predominance condition, five …pe… with respect to mutuality condition, six …pe… with respect to prenascence and repetition conditions, two …pe… with respect to non-disappearance condition, nine.

Dependent on a state that is neither of the fine-material sphere nor the immaterial sphere, there arises a state that is neither of the fine-material sphere nor the immaterial sphere by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are five; under object condition there are two … pe … under result condition there are two … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are five.
Dependent on a state that is not included [in the mundane], there arises a state that is included by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on a state that is not included [in the mundane], a state that is included arises by way of the root condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is both not included and not non-included, a state that is included arises by way of the root condition … one. (Abbreviated.
Under root there are five; under object, two … pe … under non-disappearance, five.
Dependent on a state that is not leading to liberation, a state that does not lead to liberation arises by way of the root condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is not leading to liberation, a state that does not lead to liberation arises by way of the root condition … three.
Dependent on a state that is both not leading to liberation and not leading to liberation, a state that does not lead to liberation arises by way of the root condition … one. (Abbreviated.)
Under the root condition, five; under the object condition, one ... pe ... under the result condition, one ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition, five.
Dependent on a state that is not fixed, a state that is not fixed arises by way of the root condition ... one.
Dependent on a state that is not not-fixed, a state that is not fixed arises by way of the root condition ... three.
Dependent on a state that is both indeterminate and non-indeterminate, an indeterminate state arises by way of root condition … one. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are five; under object condition there are two … pe … under resultant condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are five.
Dependent on a state that is not unsurpassed, a state that is surpassable arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is not unsurpassed … [and so forth].
Dependent on the unsurpassed state, the unsurpassed state arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on the unsurpassed state, both surpassable and unsurpassed states arise by way of root-condition… three.
Dependent on the non-unsurpassed state, the surpassable state arises by way of root-condition… one.
Dependent on a state that is both with-surpassable and not unsurpassable, a state that is with-surpassable arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are five; under object condition there are two … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are five.
